newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU aims for cattle passport, labels deal in March.
newsitem.headline: EU aims for cattle passport, labels deal in March.

text.p: European Union farm ministers on Monday made progress on proposed cattle passport and beef labelling schemes and plan to tie up an agreement in March, a European Commission spokesman said on Monday.

The proposals are intended to tighten health controls and restore consumer confidence after the British government triggered a health scare last March when it said that mad cow disease could spread to humans who ate infected beef
"They are not far away from agreement. Substantial progress has been made," agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely told reporters.
Agreement is not possible until after the European Parliament gives an opinion, expected later this week.
Kiely said one of the main obstacles was disagreement over whether beef labelling should be voluntary or compulsory.
But he said that several member states were now prepared to accept a voluntary beef labelling scheme provided it was made compulsory towards the end of the century.
Six member states, including Germany and France, oppose the Commission's proposal for a voluntary system.
There is also disagreement over whether the label should include the country or region of birth as well as information on fattening and slaughtering.
Cattle passports would be one means, along with eartags, computer data bases and registers, of identifying and registering cattle movements from birth.
Officials said there were technical problems concerning financing, number and type of eartags and deadlines for transmitting data.
Some 15-million-Ecus ($17.2 million) would be provided from existing farm funds to help set up national computer data bases over the next five years. ($ = 0.870 European Currency Unit ECUs)
